Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The failing test `testCoreFunctions` in `CoreFunctionTest` is testing core rounding functions like `round`, `floor`, and `ceiling`. The test is using `assertXPathValue` to evaluate XPath expressions involving these functions. 

The current bug report mentions that core rounding functions don't handle `NaN` or infinite values correctly. Specifically, it mentions issues with `floor` and `ceiling` functions when used with `NaN`, `Double.NEGATIVE_INFINITY`, and `Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY`.

Looking at the test method, it specifically tests the `round` function with the argument `'NaN'` and expects a result of `new Double(Double.NaN)`. This is consistent with the reported issue related to handling `NaN` values.

To trace the issue back to the code, we need to look into the implementation of the core rounding functions and their handling of special values like `NaN` and infinite values. The `CoreFunction` class seems to be involved in handling functions in JXPath expressions, including the rounding functions.

The current implementation of the core functions may not be handling special values like `NaN` correctly, leading to the test failures observed in the report. To fix the issue, adjustments need to be made in the `CoreFunction` class to handle these special cases appropriately.

Next, I will provide the methods that should be fixed to address this issue.
`org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.CoreFunction.CoreFunction(int, org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.Expression[])`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
